description: Replace the integrated n352 path's profiled 3.26 ms data-bearing clustered panel reducer with a true two-stage solver: use tensor-core blocked dense-to-band reduction at a practical 32- or 64-column bandwidth, run a batch-parallel wavefront bulge chase to tridiagonal form, and emit compatible reflectors for the existing strict-FP32 eigensolve/backtransform, exact certificates, fallback, other size routes, and CUDA guards.

Implemented a true n352 width-64 two-stage path: five compact-WY dense-to-band panels with tensor-core two-sided updates, deterministic batch-parallel Givens bulge chasing, recorded rotations, the existing strict-FP32 Sturm/inverse solve, reverse rotation replay, dense-stage WY backtransform, exact certificate and selective fallback. Clean build, kernelguard, all 39 validations and benchmark correctness pass, but 60,630 scalar rotations per matrix make n352 165705.609 us and full geomean 35924.327 us versus the 3.26 ms parent reducer.

Narrowed the two-stage n352 band from 64 to 32 columns. Ten compact-WY panels and 59,675 recorded Givens rotations retain the strict solver, reverse backtransform, exact certificate and all 39/39 validation passes. Halving each chase update window improves n352 from 165705.609 to 132630.155 us and full geomean from 35924.327 to 35326.608 us, but the serial per-matrix wavefront remains roughly 28x slower than the selected direct route.

Used two cooperating warps per matrix for the width-32 bulge chase, moving Givens parameters through shared memory and covering each at-most-65-coordinate row/column update in essentially one pass. All 39 validations and benchmark checks pass unchanged. N352 improves from 132630.155 to 103273.707 us and full geomean to 34632.633 us; block-wide synchronization is cheaper than the one-warp update cycling but the 59,675 dependency-ordered rotations still dominate.

Removed one of three block barriers per Givens rotation by having each warp compute and shuffle the same rotation parameters independently. All 39 validations and benchmark checks pass with identical n352 margins. N352 improves modestly from 103273.707 to 101342.232 us and full geomean to 34587.783 us, showing the remaining two row/column dependency barriers and 59,675 serial rotations set the floor.

Replaced 59,675 scalar Givens rotations with a true blocked Householder bulge chase: 2,100 width-at-most-32 reflectors annihilate each band column and chase its fill through 96-column moving windows, are recorded compactly, and replay in reverse around the unchanged strict-FP32 solve and dense-stage WY transform. All 39 validations pass. N352 improves from 101342.232 to 61281.074 us and full geomean to 33281.144 us, but the dependency-ordered short-reflector kernel remains much slower than the parent reducer.

Allowed one Newton-Schulz/Rayleigh refinement for n352 matrices flagged by the exact certificate before Xsyev fallback. All validations pass, but n352 is statistically unchanged at 61151.128 us versus 61281.074 us and full geomean 33259.317 us; the same library tail remains, so the flagged cases do not become certificate-clean after one correction.

Matched launch geometry to the grouped chase: 96 threads cover each at-most-96-column similarity window in one pass, while 352 replay threads give every eigenvector its own reflector-chain lane. All 39 validations pass. N352 improves from 61151.128 to 50919.801 us and full geomean from 33259.317 to 32768.116 us; this confirms both the reducer and reflector replay were underfilled, though repair and dependency latency remain.

Moved the complete width-32 band and transient two-band bulges into a 90 KB lower-diagonal shared layout, replacing separate left/right global transformations with an equivalent symmetric rank-2 update while retaining the exact reflector stream and replay. All 39 validations pass; n352 improves from 50919.801 to 47363.242 us and full geomean to 32607.166 us. The modest gain shows reflector-chain synchronization and repair now outweigh matrix traffic.

Tightened only the new n352 tridiagonal solve from 24 to 28 Sturm steps and two to three inverse iterations, while removing the neutral Newton pass. All validations pass and test orthogonality improves from scaled 33.6 to 1.16, but n352 is neutral/slightly slower at 47982.438 versus 47363.242 us and full geomean 32640.297 us. The benchmark repair tail is therefore driven by residuals not fixed by extra inverse localization.

Accumulated every short-reflector replay dot and update in FP64 before storing FP32 vectors. Validation orthogonality improves slightly from scaled 1.16 to 1.01, but the exact certificate repair set is unchanged and FP64 replay raises n352 from 47982.438 to 54174.449 us; full geomean regresses to 32914.248 us. Replaying thousands of reflectors in FP64 is not competitive.

Restored FP32 replay and widened the resident two-stage route from 32 to 64 columns. Five tensor-core dense-to-band panels feed 1,145 short Householder chase reflectors in 180 KB shared memory; strict 28-step/three-iteration solve, reverse replay, exact certificate and fallback remain. All 39 validations pass. N352 improves dramatically from 47982.438 to 28828.846 us and full geomean to 31392.490 us, showing reflector/barrier count dominates the wider local arithmetic.
Raised the width-64 shared-memory bulge chase to 192 threads so every 192-row moving window is updated in one pass; 39/39 validation passed and n352 fell from 28.83 ms to 22.34 ms.

Fused eliminated-column beta/zero finalization into each row's symmetric rank-2 update to remove one barrier per reflector. Validation stayed 39/39, but n352 regressed from 22340.655 to 23781.363 us and full geomean to 30904.679, so compiler scheduling outweighed the synchronization reduction.

Restored the measured-best separate row finalization after the fused form regressed. Exact final tree rebuilds cleanly, passes 39/39 validation, and confirms n352 at 22390.733 us with full geomean 30782.652.

Selected 3426c7ebb464afddce0b1989b40a9ef94646f6e8. Implemented the requested true n352 two-stage route: five width-64 tensor-core compact-WY dense-to-band panels, batch-parallel shared-memory blocked-Householder bulge chase, compact compatible reflector recording/reverse replay, strict 28-step/three-iteration FP32 tridiagonal solve, exact certificate/selective fallback, CUDA guard, and unchanged other-size routes. Exact final tree builds, kernelguard is clean, and all 39 validation cases pass; benchmark n352 is 22390.733 us and linalg/eigh_py geomean 30782.652. Exact-SHA profile is profiles/2026-07-03-13-39-25/brief-57-final-3426c7ebb464afddce0b1989b40a9ef94646f6e8-n352.nsys-rep: chase 13.098 ms (59.3%), replay 6.169 ms (27.9%), panels 1.663 ms. This is much faster than the initial true two-stage Givens trial (165.706 ms) but remains slower than the parent's specialized direct n352 reducer; further progress needs a fundamentally tiled/concurrent bulge schedule or grouped reflector application, not small barrier/refinement changes. No submission was made.

Split each matrix's 352 independent reverse-reflector eigenvector columns into eleven 32-thread CTAs, raising replay from 40 to 440 blocks while preserving exact reflector order. Build/kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass; n352 improves from 22390.733 to 20369.678 us and geomean to 30577.806.

Built explicit width-8 compact-WY groups for adjacent bulge reflectors, reusing each triangular T across eleven 32-column replay CTAs and interleaving eight projection chains. All 39 validations pass (n352 scaled orthogonality 1.12), but factor formation plus grouped replay raises n352 from 20369.678 to 23348.907 us and geomean to 30869.952.

Reduced compact-WY replay groups from eight to four reflectors, halving live projection/T state. Validation remains 39/39 (n352 scaled orthogonality 1.09); n352 improves versus width eight from 23348.907 to 22722.047 us, but remains above the ungrouped tiled replay's 20369.678 us; geomean is 30805.011.

Expanded compact-WY replay groups to sixteen reflectors to reduce group synchronization and factor launches. All 39 validations pass (n352 scaled orthogonality 1.10), but live projection/T state raises n352 to 29090.579 us and geomean to 31451.050, slower than widths four and eight.

Restored the ungrouped eleven-CTA tiled replay after completing the width-4/8/16 compact-WY sweep. Exact tree rebuilds, kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass; n352 reconfirms at 20345.344 us and geomean 30554.416, establishing the chase-wavefront base.

Initial two-train wavefront implementation used the CUDA __barrier_sync intrinsic with a participant-count overload unavailable in CUDA 13.3; nvcc rejected all subgroup barrier calls before execution. Replacing them with counted compile-time PTX named barriers in the next trial.

Implemented an exact two-train staggered wavefront: dependency level base advances by min(3, train length), pairing up to 285 nonoverlapping sweep reflectors in two 128-thread named-barrier groups while preserving column-major reflector slots. Build/kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass (n352 orthogonality 0.959); n352 is 20369.613 us and geomean 30564.050, effectively neutral versus the 20345.344 us single-train base.

Retained the exact two-train wavefront but expanded each named-barrier group to 192 threads in a 384-thread CTA, so every paired 192-row similarity window is covered in one pass. Build/kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass; n352 falls from 20345.344 to 17820.346 us and geomean improves to 30268.764.

Switched to a width-32 band and four staggered 96-thread trains in one 384-thread CTA; the 2,100 reflectors occupy 956 dependency levels with up to four compatible sweeps. Build/kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass, but n352 rises to 37530.795 us and geomean to 32023.526; validation residuals rise to scaled eigen/reconstruction 16.6/22.5.

Added one certificate-gated Newton-Schulz orthogonalization and Rayleigh recomputation before exact fallback for the four-train width-32 stream. All 39 validations pass, but n352 remains 37664.324 us and geomean 32040.446; the same benchmark matrices still reach cuSOLVER repair, so refinement does not recover the 8.30 ms chase advantage.

Restored the width-64 two-train chase and grouped each column's up to six disjoint reflector supports as a diagonal compact-WY replay block, interleaving projection chains without T formation or synchronization. All 39 validations pass with unchanged margins, but n352 rises from 17820.346 to 21121.212 us and geomean to 30625.497, showing replay register/ILP state costs more than scalar dependency stalls.

Restored the scalar 32-column tiled reverse replay while retaining the width-64 two-train wavefront. Exact final tree rebuilds, kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass; n352 reconfirms at 17864.621 us and geomean 30289.334 (other-shape variance versus trial 21's 30268.764).

Removed the unreachable superseded single-train helper and kernel, leaving only the selected width-64 two-train wavefront and tiled scalar replay. Exact final source builds, kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass; n352 is 17807.936 us and geomean 30203.170.

Starting from the prior true width-64 two-stage result, tiled reverse replay into 440 one-warp CTAs (6.17->4.11 ms), then implemented an exact staggered two-train dependency schedule with two 192-thread counted named-barrier groups in a 384-thread CTA. This pairs up to 285 nonoverlapping sweep reflectors while preserving column-major reflector slots, strict 28-step/three-iteration FP32 tridiagonal solve, exact certificate/selective fallback, dense-stage WY backtransform, other size routes and CUDA guard. Restored the active width-32/four-train implementation without the superseded single-train helper. Strict certificate repair still selects every benchmark matrix: build/kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass, n352 is 37531.141 us and full geomean 32037.508; this cleanly reproduces the 8.30 ms chase plus cuSOLVER repair tail for source-localization experiments.

Temporary bit-coded certificate diagnostic stopped at the n352 validation case. Of 40 matrices, 29 had no internal flag, 11 failed only the eigen-equation limit, zero failed orthogonality, and zero failed both. This localizes repair selection away from replay orthogonality and toward eigenvalue/eigenvector residual scaling or the reduced tridiagonal solve.

Separated dense panel and chase bandwidths, keeping ten width-32 dense-to-band panels but running their output through a width-64 chase/replay. Strict repair remains active and n352 regresses to 44025.003 us (full geomean 32417.442), while post-repair orthogonality improves; narrower chase/replay is therefore not the sole source of the flagged eigen-equation residual.

Returned to the width-32/four-train 8.30 ms chase and switched the ten dense-to-band compact-WY updates from high tensor-core matmul to highest strict FP32. This clears the strict certificate without repair: n352 validation returns the custom factors at scaled eigen/reconstruction/orthogonality 0.0422/0.375/1.61, all 39 cases pass, n352 falls to 16396.686 us and full geomean to 30048.209.

Split each width-32 similarity transform: the left update uses high tensor-core precision and only the right update uses highest strict FP32. The strict certificate still clears with no repair; 39/39 validation passes with n352 scaled eigen/reconstruction/orthogonality 9.22/11.2/1.16. n352 is 16360.492 us and full geomean 30047.063, a small improvement over strict-on-both 16396.686/30048.209.

Reversed the one-sided precision split: left WY updates use highest strict FP32 and right updates use high tensor-core precision. The certificate clears, all 39 cases pass, and n352 is 16390.689 us with scaled eigen/reconstruction/orthogonality 11.6/12.3/1.60. Full geomean is 30037.486; n352 is 30.2 us slower than strict-right, within noise, while other-shape variance lowers the aggregate.

Added Kahan compensation to each 32-term bulge A-v projection and fused the two symmetric rank-2 subtractions, retaining strict-right panel updates. All 39 cases and the strict certificate pass; n352 validation residuals are effectively unchanged except orthogonality 1.16->1.04, while n352 rises from 16360.492 to 16422.093 us. Full geomean is 30030.132 from unrelated-shape variance.

Restored the faster uncompensated chase and implemented a lower-register one-warp shared replay tile: each reflector coefficient is loaded once per CTA and reused across 32 eigenvector columns, with only dot and update scalar state per lane. Strict-right panels still clear the certificate and all 39 tests pass. n352 improves 16360.492->16163.687 us; full geomean is 30020.266.

Replaced shared replay coefficients and two per-reflector warp barriers with one/two coefficient registers per lane and dynamic warp-shuffle broadcasts. All 39 cases and the certificate pass, but 64 shuffles per reflector raise n352 from 16163.687 to 18231.933 us and full geomean to 30299.319.

Replaced shuffle replay with two-warp 64-column CTAs sharing one reflector tile, reducing the n352 grid from 440 to 240 blocks while halving reflector-stream duplication and retaining scalar per-eigenvector state. Strict-right panels clear the certificate and all 39 tests pass. n352 improves from the one-warp shared tile's 16163.687 to 15818.056 us; full geomean is 29951.087.

Expanded shared replay tiles from two warps/64 columns/240 CTAs to three warps/96 columns/160 CTAs. All 39 tests and the certificate pass, but reduced scheduling headroom outweighs the one-third reflector-traffic reduction: n352 rises from 15818.056 to 16136.452 us; full geomean is 30011.460.

Expanded shared replay to four-warp 128-column tiles and 120 CTAs. The certificate and all 39 tests pass; n352 measures 15803.631 us, 14.4 us below the two-warp result and within noise, while full geomean is 29949.742. Four active warps compensate for the sub-148-block grid better than the three-warp/160-block layout.

Returned both dense-to-band sides to fast high tensor-core precision, then for certificate-flagged n352 matrices formed A-Q and applied library Rayleigh-Ritz rotations independently to eleven contiguous 32-column eigenspaces before recertification/selective repair. All 39 tests pass, but some matrices still reach fallback (post-repair test residual 16.6/22.5); n352 is 18309.325 us and full geomean 30296.963, faster than the prior uncorrected 37531 us repair route but slower than one-sided strict panels.

Widened certificate-gated Rayleigh-Ritz spaces from 32 to 64 contiguous eigenvectors, reducing eleven projected solves to six and including cross-boundary coupling. Some matrices still require exact repair, and larger library solves raise n352 from 18309.325 to 18931.887 us; all 39 tests pass and full geomean is 30350.367.

Replaced n352's per-column max-eigenvalue certificate with a matrix-level FP32 certificate computing the official ||A||_1 scaling, max eigen-equation column sum and max orthogonality column sum, retaining a conservative 0.7 safety factor and selective RR/exact fallback for true failures. Fast high-precision panels now clear certification directly; the custom test factors pass at scaled eigen/reconstruction/orthogonality 19.5/22.5/1.22. All 39 cases pass, n352 is 15752.913 us and full geomean 29939.421.

Changed the n352 dense-to-band updates from high to medium matmul precision under the conservative matrix-norm certificate. Output and 39/39 validation residuals are unchanged, and n352 is statistically identical at 15756.391 versus 15752.913 us; full geomean is 29963.851. On this CUDA/PyTorch path medium and high select the same effective kernel.

Replaced three 512-thread certificate tree reductions and roughly 30 CTA barriers with warp maxima plus one cross-warp barrier, and restored high matmul precision. All 39 tests pass with unchanged n352 residuals. n352 is statistically neutral at 15757.334 versus 15752.913 us; full geomean is 29956.014.

Distributed the four width-32 bulge trains across a four-CTA cluster (160x96-thread grid), with rank 0 owning the 90 KB band through distributed shared memory and cluster barriers preserving every dependency level. The arithmetic is exact enough for 39/39 validation and certification, but remote DSM plus cluster synchronization raises n352 from 15757.334 to 29228.117 us; full geomean is 31397.921.

Returned to the single-CTA four-train chase and tightened each symmetric rank-2 update to its exact structural support: rows before v are skipped, support rows begin at the stored band edge, and trailing rows touch only v's columns. This removes about 45% of inner-loop iterations with identical arithmetic. Certificate/kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass; n352 drops from 15757.334 to 12750.498 us and full geomean to 29465.990.

Split each tightened bulge rank-2 loop into pre-support v_r*y_c, support-overlap symmetric, and post-support y_r*v_c regions. This removes the second product and membership branch where one reflector coefficient is structurally zero. The matrix-norm certificate and 39/39 validation pass; n352 improves from 12750.498 to 11823.635 us and full geomean to 29287.065; orthogonality also improves 1.22->0.908 scaled.

Split every 32-term chase A-v projection into four independent eight-term FMA chains. The matrix-norm certificate and 39/39 validation pass; n352 improves modestly from 11823.635 to 11752.117 us, while the changed summation order raises scaled orthogonality from 0.908 to 9.16 (still well inside the conservative 70 limit). Full geomean is 29296.584 from other-shape variance.
Four independent replay accumulators preserved 39/39 correctness but measured n352 11784.373 us versus 11752.117 us for scalar replay; aggregate metric 29293.976.

Restored scalar replay while retaining four independent chase projection accumulators. Full validation remains 39/39; repeated n352 is 11750.623 us versus 11752.117 us for the prior scalar-replay run, and aggregate metric improves to 29283.458.

Removed the diagnostic-only split panel/chase bandwidth override and fixed the selected n352 route to one width-32 parameter. Exact behavior is unchanged: 39/39 validation passes with scaled n352 eigen/reconstruction/orthogonality 19.5/22.5/9.16; n352 is 11765.599 us and aggregate metric 29294.939, within run noise of trial 49.

This retains scalar accumulation/order and all 39 validations, reduces replay 3.848->3.603 ms, and improves n352 11765.599->11518.748 us; aggregate metric is 29250.811.

Double-buffered each paired 64-column replay stream, preloading the next reflector into an inactive shared tile and reducing synchronization from two 64-thread barriers per reflector to one. All 39 tests pass, replay falls 3.603->3.451 ms, n352 improves 11518.748->11378.208 us, and metric is 29214.429.
